title: Continuous inverse-limit Cech primitive with prescribed first reduction
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $q:T\to S$ be a continuous surjection of profinite spaces, meaning compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces. For $r\geq1$, let $P_r=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})\in T^r:q(t_i)=q(t_j)\text{ for all }i,j\}$ with the subspace topology, as in [def-sfb-profinite-cech-tuples]. For a topological abelian group $M$, write $C^k(M)=C(P_{k+1},M)$ for all continuous maps, with pointwise addition, and for $k\geq0$ define
$$(d_k^M c)(t_0,\ldots,t_{k+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{k+1}),$$
where the signs act by the additive group law. Let $(A_m,p_m)_{m\geq1}$ be a sequence of finite discrete abelian groups and surjective homomorphisms $p_m:A_{m+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_m$. Give
$$L=\{(x_m)\in\prod_{m\geq1}A_m:p_m(x_{m+1})=x_m\text{ for all }m\geq1\}$$
the subspace topology of the product and coordinatewise addition, and write $\rho_m:L\to A_m$ for the projections. Fix $n\geq1$, a continuous $f\in C^n(L)$ satisfying $d_n^L f=0$, and a prescribed $u_1\in C^{n-1}(A_1)$ satisfying $d_{n-1}^{A_1}u_1=\rho_1\circ f$. Then there exists a continuous $u\in C^{n-1}(L)$ such that
$$d_{n-1}^L u=f,\qquad \rho_1\circ u=u_1.$$
Equivalently, its reductions $u_m=\rho_m\circ u$ satisfy $p_m\circ u_{m+1}=u_m$ and $d_{n-1}^{A_m}u_m=\rho_m\circ f$ for every $m\geq1$. Empty spaces and zero groups are included. The conclusion concerns actual continuous maps into the specified inverse-limit topology.

proof.text: Put $f_m=\rho_m\circ f$. Each $\rho_m$ is continuous, being a product projection restricted to $L$, so $f_m$ is continuous. An additive homomorphism $a:M\to N$ commutes with every finite signed sum, hence $d_k^N(a\circ c)=a\circ d_k^M c$. In particular $d_n^{A_m}f_m=0$ and $p_m\circ f_{m+1}=f_m$ for every $m\geq1$, the latter equality being a defining equation of $L$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), agent expansion of the compatible coefficient tower: coordinate naturality.

proof.text: For each $m\geq1$ let $X_m$ be the set of continuous $w:P_n\to A_m$ satisfying $d_{n-1}^{A_m}w=f_m$. The prescribed $u_1$ belongs to $X_1$. For every $w\in X_m$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-coefficient-cech-primitive-lift] with the same $q:T\to S$, the same positive $n$, $A=A_m$, $B=A_{m+1}$, $p=p_m$, $c=f_{m+1}$ and prescribed primitive $w$. The tuple spaces and differentials in that statement are exactly the ones here. Both groups are finite discrete, $p_m$ is surjective, $f_{m+1}$ is a continuous cocycle, and $d_{n-1}^{A_m}w=f_m=p_m\circ f_{m+1}$. It gives $v\in X_{m+1}$ with $p_m\circ v=w$. Choose such a successor for each pair $(m,w)$. Recursion starting at the given $u_1$ then extends a finite family $(u_1,\ldots,u_m)$ by this successor of its last entry. Its invariant is $u_i\in X_i$ for $1\leq i\leq m$, $p_i\circ u_{i+1}=u_i$ for $1\leq i<m$, and first entry equal to the prescribed $u_1$. The base case was checked; appending $v$ preserves the old entries and adds precisely the two equations just obtained. Thus the resulting sequence has all the required equations for every $m\geq1$ and retains the prescribed first entry.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2),(4), agent expansion: compatible primitive induction using the existing finite-coefficient lifting statement.

proof.text: Define $u(x)=(u_m(x))_{m\geq1}$ for $x\in P_n$. The compatibility just proved puts this tuple in the specified subset $L$. A basic open set of $L$ is the intersection with $L$ of a finite-coordinate cylinder $\bigcap_{m\in F}\operatorname{pr}_m^{-1}(V_m)$, with $F$ finite and each $V_m\subset A_m$ open. Its inverse image under $u$ is $\bigcap_{m\in F}u_m^{-1}(V_m)$, an open set. Arbitrary opens are unions of such basic opens, so $u:P_n\to L$ is continuous for exactly the topology in the statement.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(4), agent expansion of inverse-limit reconstruction: explicit subspace/product basis calculation.

proof.text: For every $m\geq1$, evaluate the displayed differential coordinatewise: $\rho_m\circ d_{n-1}^L u=d_{n-1}^{A_m}(\rho_m\circ u)=d_{n-1}^{A_m}u_m=f_m=\rho_m\circ f$. Two elements of $L$ are equal precisely when all their coordinates agree, so $d_{n-1}^L u=f$. Construction gives $\rho_1\circ u=u_1$ and every claimed reduction identity. Conversely reductions of any such $u$ satisfy these identities by the defining equations of $L$ and the same finite-sum calculation. If $T=S=\varnothing$, all domains $P_n$ used here are empty since $n\geq1$, and the unique maps give the conclusion; zero groups also cause no exception.
